sources.entry: Reactive Resume - One-of-a-kind resume builder that keeps your privacy in mind. Completely secure, customizable and portable. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Reactive Resume is a free, open-source, self-hostable resume and cover letter builder with live preview, resume checks, job application tracking, and an optional AI assistant.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you write resumes and cover letters in a visual editor with a live PDF preview, and export them as PDF, Word (DOCX), Markdown, or JSON. It offers 18 templates with customization options for fonts, colors, spacing, paper size, and sidebars. Resume checks include readability findings, job-posting keyword matching, and a public ATS checker that reads PDFs in the browser. A job application tracker has List, Board, Insights, and Calendar views, and can tailor a resume for a saved job. Imports cover Reactive Resume JSON, JSON Resume, LinkedIn data exports, PDF, and Word files. The README also describes a REST API and MCP server, public share links with optional passwords, and an optional AI assistant that works with providers you connect.
use_cases: check a resume against a job posting
share a resume through a public link
how_to_run: Edit .env to set AUTH_SECRET and a separate ENCRYPTION_SECRET (generate each with: openssl rand -hex 32)
notable: Self-hostable with Docker, Kubernetes, Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, or a Hostinger one-click template
PDF rendering via Forme in the browser and on the server, with no Chromium or external print service required
REST API and MCP server for scripts and external assistants
Optional AI assistant with proposed edits you can accept or reject; supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, and others
MIT licensed with no tracking, ads, or paid tier
caveats: Optional AI features and hosting may incur costs from the provider or host
Cloudflare deployment requires the Workers Paid plan and an existing PostgreSQL database
Upgrading from v5 requires backups, stopping v5 instances, and manual conversion of old visual style rules
